items.title: Harry "Sweets" Edison interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I did everything with him and Nelson Riddle for about 13 years.

ctx.x: How many years did you spend with the Basie band?

Well from ‘38 until 1950, then I went back and I got a studio job here at ABC, with Mitchell Ayres on the Hollywood Palace, and then I started playing with Frank Sinatra. I did everything with him and Nelson Riddle for about 13 years. I recorded a lot with Nat King Cole, Ella Fitzgerald. I’ve been blessed all my life. It seems like that I don’t know why I’ve been called to do records that like anybody could have done it you know.

Yeah, but like you stated, you had your sound. You must have developed a sound that people recognized and that when Frank Sinatra did a date, he knew who he wanted to hear behind him, as did Nelson Riddle.

items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: When we first started, Nelson would write me a couple of bars behind him, fill-ins you know.

ctx.x: Yeah. I started making some records…I think the first record I made with Nelson was with Frank Sinatra, I think the record was “Wee Hours”. I think that’s one of the best he’s ever made. I think that was just absolutely a fresh album, his voice was fresh. Then we became very close friends and he always wanted me on his albums. When we first started, Nelson would write me a couple of bars behind him, fill-ins you know. Then it got to the point where he would have five trumpets instead of four and I would just put…
So you wouldn’t have to play a part, just be a soloist and play obbligatos.

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: Oh, yes, my first record date out here was with Nelson Riddle, you know.

ctx.x: But it was really Nelson Riddle who started you,
Oh, yes, my first record date out here was with Nelson Riddle, you know. And then after that, I started

I started playing with Frank Sinatra in 1952. And the first album I made with him was "Wee Hours". That was on his comeback, you know. Comeback at that time. His popularity had diminished. I don't know for what reason but he hadn't sang in a long time, you know. He'd been active in the movies and --
